terms.meaning: A Python framework for building web APIs.
The server program that runs the FastAPI app.
A layer that decides which websites may call the backend.
A group of routes that is added to the app together.
Code that runs when the app starts and when it stops.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the app
sections.what: Loads the web framework, CORS and lifespan tools, the two route modules, the settings, and the logger.
sections.why: Likely reason: needed to build the app and connect its routes.

sections.name: lifespan
sections.title: App setup, logging and routes
sections.what: Defines what runs at start and stop, creates the app with its title, applies the cross-origin rule from settings, and connects the agent and export routes under the /api/v1 prefix.
sections.why: Likely reason: the start log shows the settings so a developer can confirm them.
sections.watch_out: The cross-origin rule comes from the settings, and the wildcard default lets any website call the backend.

sections.name: root
sections.title: Root status route
sections.what: Returns the app name, version, and a running status at the root address.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives a quick check that the server is up.
sections.watch_out: The version here is typed separately from the other version copies.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Direct run option
sections.what: When the file is started directly, runs the server with the host, port, and log level from settings.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a developer start the server with one command.
sections.watch_out: Auto-reload restarts the server when files change, which is meant for development and not for real deployment.

summary: Starts the web application: it builds the app, applies the cross-origin rule, connects the routes, and can run the server when the file is started directly.
purpose: Is the entry point that the server loads to serve the API.
why: Likely reason: one file assembles the whole app.
how: Creates the app with a title and start and stop logging, applies the CORS rule from settings, includes the agent and export routes under the /api/v1 prefix, adds a root check, and runs the server if the file is started directly.
inputs: Settings values and the route modules.
outputs: A running web server on the configured host and port.
risks: The direct run option turns on auto-reload, which is meant for development. The CORS rule allows any website when the setting is the wildcard. The Docker start command may not match how this file imports its modules.
debug: Check the start log for the vector store path. If /api/v1 addresses return 404, check the router prefix. If startup reports an attempted relative import, start the server from the folder above the backend package.
